## Case 1. A very fast prototype

**Lens:** A curious invention. **Regions:** Europe. **Era:** modern. **Reveal form:** Object drawing: tap the parts. **Difficulty:** entry.

**Question.** In which year did the first Concorde prototype make its first flight?

**Answer: 1969.** First flight of Concorde prototype 001 from Toulouse

- Definition: The year of the first flight of prototype 001, not of supersonic flight (1 October 1969) and not of passenger service (1976).
- Precision: day known (2 March); year used. Calendar: Gregorian.
- Discovery versus event: Event: first flight. Not the first supersonic flight, not certification, not scheduled service.
- Corridor: 1960 to 1985.


**Free evidence** (what every player sees)

- *bound* By the end of that year, the Boeing 737 had already made its first flight (9 April 1967).  
  Anchor: Boeing 737 first flight, 9 April 1967. Sources: [Boeing 737 (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_737). Level **V1**.
- *bound* By the end of that year, the Boeing 747 had not yet carried passengers (first passenger service 22 January 1970).  
  Anchor: Boeing 747 enters passenger service, 22 January 1970. Sources: [Boeing 747 (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747). Level **V1**.
- *relation* It flew one calendar year after Apollo 8 first took people into lunar orbit (21 to 27 December 1968).  
  Anchor: Apollo 8 lunar orbit mission, 21-27 December 1968. Sources: [Apollo 8 (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_8). Level **V1**.

**Candidates after the two free bounds (C0):** 1967, 1968, 1969 (3 years).

**Uniqueness proof** (why only 1969 survives the relation):

- 1967 is -1 calendar years from Apollo 8 lunar orbit mission (1968); the clue needs +1.
- 1968 is +0 calendar years from Apollo 8 lunar orbit mission (1968); the clue needs +1.

**Paid clues**

- Nudge, 1 Insight, category *Aviation*: By the end of that year, the Boeing 737 had already entered airline service (10 February 1968).  
  Cuts 1967 from C0, leaves 2.  Sources: [Boeing 737 (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_737). Level **V1**.
- Deep, 2 Insight, category *Aviation*: By the end of that year, the Boeing 747 had already made its first flight (9 February 1969).  
  Cuts 1967, 1968 from C0, leaves 1. It resolves the case. Sources: [Boeing 747 (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_747). Level **V1**.

**Free context (cuts nothing):** Concorde entered scheduled passenger service on 21 January 1976.


**Sample player explanation (free evidence only, zero Insight)**

1. The two dated anchors give a corridor of 1967 to 1969. The 737 had flown by 1967, and the 747 was not yet carrying passengers by the end of the year in question (that happened in January 1970).
2. The third fragment says one calendar year after Apollo 8, which was in December 1968. One year after 1968 is 1969.
3. 1967 and 1968 fail the third fragment. Lock 1969.

**If the player misses.** 1967 and 1968 fit the two bounds, but only 1969 is one calendar year after Apollo 8 (December 1968). The date known to historians is 2 March 1969.

**Reveal.** Form: Object drawing: tap the parts.

- *Prototype 001, F-WTSS* (Object drawing): Concorde 001 first flew from Toulouse on 2 March 1969 with André Turcat at the controls. It first went supersonic on 1 October 1969. Sources: [Concorde (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concorde).

## Case 2. The first nation where women voted

**Lens:** A political turning point. **Regions:** Oceania. **Era:** modern. **Reveal form:** Annotated timeline of petitions, law and first vote. **Difficulty:** entry.

**Question.** In which year did New Zealand pass the law giving women the right to vote in parliamentary elections?

**Answer: 1893.** Royal assent to the Electoral Act 1893 (19 September 1893)

- Definition: The year the Act received royal assent. Women first voted in the general election of 28 November 1893, the same year. Women could vote before they could stand for Parliament; this case is about the vote.
- Precision: day known (19 September); year used. Calendar: Gregorian.
- Discovery versus event: Event: assent to the Act. Not the first vote, and not women standing for Parliament.
- Corridor: 1880 to 1905.


**Free evidence** (what every player sees)

- *bound* By the end of that year, the Eiffel Tower had been completed in Paris (31 March 1889).  
  Anchor: Eiffel Tower completed, 31 March 1889. Sources: [Eiffel Tower (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower). Level **V1**.
- *bound* By the end of that year, the Lumière brothers had not yet held their first paid public film screening (28 December 1895).  
  Anchor: Lumière first paid screening, 28 December 1895. Sources: [Lumière brothers (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumi%C3%A8re_brothers). Level **V1**.
- *relation* It happened one calendar year after the second of three suffrage petitions was delivered to Parliament (1892).  
  Anchor: Second suffrage petition delivered to Parliament, 1892. Sources: [Women's suffrage in New Zealand (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_suffrage_in_New_Zealand). Level **V1**.

**Candidates after the two free bounds (C0):** 1889, 1890, 1891, 1892, 1893, 1894 (6 years).

**Uniqueness proof** (why only 1893 survives the relation):

- 1889 is -3 calendar years from Second suffrage petition delivered to Parliament (1892); the clue needs +1.
- 1890 is -2 calendar years from Second suffrage petition delivered to Parliament (1892); the clue needs +1.
- 1891 is -1 calendar years from Second suffrage petition delivered to Parliament (1892); the clue needs +1.
- 1892 is +0 calendar years from Second suffrage petition delivered to Parliament (1892); the clue needs +1.
- 1894 is +2 calendar years from Second suffrage petition delivered to Parliament (1892); the clue needs +1.

**Paid clues**

- Nudge, 1 Insight, category *Politics*: By the end of that year, the first suffrage petition had already been delivered to Parliament (1891).  
  Cuts 1889, 1890 from C0, leaves 4.  Sources: [Women's suffrage in New Zealand (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_suffrage_in_New_Zealand). Level **V1**.
- Deep, 2 Insight, category *World events*: By the end of that year, the World's Columbian Exposition had opened in Chicago (1 May 1893).  
  Cuts 1889, 1890, 1891, 1892 from C0, leaves 2.  Sources: [World's Columbian Exposition (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World%27s_Columbian_Exposition). Level **V1**.

1. The Eiffel Tower is 1889 and the first Lumière screening is 1895. The Act must be after 1889 and before 1895, so 1889 to 1894.
2. The petition of almost 20,000 signatures was in 1892. The third fragment says one calendar year after that, so 1893.

- *Three petitions, one law* (Timeline): Petitions were delivered to Parliament in 1891, 1892 and 1893, each larger than the one before (counts HOLD). The Act received royal assent on 19 September 1893. Sources: [Women's suffrage in New Zealand (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_suffrage_in_New_Zealand).
- *Vote, not candidacy* (Note on terms): The 1893 Act gave women the vote. Women's right to stand for Parliament came later. The date of the law and the date of the first vote are different facts: 19 September and 28 November 1893. Sources: [Women's suffrage in New Zealand (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_suffrage_in_New_Zealand).

## Case 3. The way back across the Pacific

**Lens:** Food and trade routes. **Regions:** Asia, Americas. **Era:** early modern. **Reveal form:** Trade-route map, drawn with uncertainty. **Difficulty:** medium.

**Question.** In which year did a Spanish ship first complete the return voyage across the Pacific from the Philippines to Mexico?

**Answer: 1565.** Urdaneta's ship reaches Acapulco on 8 October 1565

- Definition: The year of arrival at Acapulco of the first successful eastbound crossing (the tornaviaje). Not the year of the outward voyage and not the year Manila became the colony's capital.
- Precision: day known (8 October); year used. Calendar: Gregorian.
- Discovery versus event: Event: the arrival that proved the return route. The route was then used until 1815.
- Corridor: 1555 to 1580.


**Free evidence** (what every player sees)

- *bound* By the end of that year, a Spanish fleet under Legazpi had already sailed from La Navidad in Mexico (21 November 1564).  
  Anchor: Legazpi's fleet sails from La Navidad, 21 November 1564. Sources: [Andrés de Urdaneta (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Urdaneta). Level **V1**.
- *bound* By the end of that year, Mercator had not yet published his world map (1569).  
  Anchor: Mercator's world map, 1569. Sources: [Mercator 1569 world map (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercator_1569_world_map). Level **V1**.
- *relation* The return voyage reached Mexico one calendar year after the fleet sailed from La Navidad.  
  Anchor: Fleet sails from La Navidad, 21 November 1564. Sources: [Andrés de Urdaneta (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Urdaneta). Level **V1**.

**Candidates after the two free bounds (C0):** 1564, 1565, 1566, 1567, 1568 (5 years).

**Uniqueness proof** (why only 1565 survives the relation):

- 1564 is +0 calendar years from Fleet sails from La Navidad (1564); the clue needs +1.
- 1566 is +2 calendar years from Fleet sails from La Navidad (1564); the clue needs +1.
- 1567 is +3 calendar years from Fleet sails from La Navidad (1564); the clue needs +1.
- 1568 is +4 calendar years from Fleet sails from La Navidad (1564); the clue needs +1.

**Paid clues**

- Nudge, 1 Insight, category *Exploration*: By the end of that year, the Spanish fleet had already reached the Philippines (Samar, 13 February 1565).  
  Cuts 1564 from C0, leaves 4.  Sources: [Andrés de Urdaneta (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Urdaneta). Level **V1**.

**Sample player explanation (free evidence only, zero Insight)**

1. The fleet sailed in November 1564, so the target is 1564 or later. Mercator's map is 1569, so the target is before that: 1564 to 1568.
2. The third fragment says one calendar year after the fleet sailed, which is 1565.
3. Lock 1565.

**If the player misses.** 1564 to 1568 fit the bounds. Only 1565 is one calendar year after the fleet sailed in November 1564.

**Reveal.** Form: Trade-route map, drawn with uncertainty.

- *Why the way back was the hard part* (Route map (schematic)): Reaching the Philippines from Mexico was the easier direction. The hard part was finding a way back. Urdaneta left Cebu on 1 June 1565 and reached Acapulco on 8 October. Sources: [Andrés de Urdaneta (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Urdaneta).
- *A route that lasted* (Trade rhythm): The Manila galleon route operated from 1565 to 1815. Sources: [Manila galleon (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_galleon).

**Facts and verification**

- [V1] Urdaneta left Cebu on 1 June 1565 and reached Acapulco on 8 October 1565. (8 October 1565; day). Opened: [Andrés de Urdaneta (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Urdaneta). Corroboration seen only in search summaries: [Manila galleon (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_galleon). Note: Several search results agree. Urdaneta's birth year is given as 1498 and 1508; not used.
- [V1] The fleet sailed from La Navidad on 21 November 1564. (21 November 1564; day). Opened: [Andrés de Urdaneta (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_de_Urdaneta). Corroboration seen only in search summaries: none.
- [V1] The route operated from 1565 to 1815. (1565 to 1815; year). Opened: [Manila galleon (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_galleon). Corroboration seen only in search summaries: none.
- [V1] The Spanish colonial capital moved to Manila in 1571. (1571; year). Opened: [Miguel López de Legazpi (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_L%C3%B3pez_de_Legazpi). Corroboration seen only in search summaries: none.

## Case 5. A slab found by soldiers

**Lens:** Archaeology: found, made, decoded. **Regions:** Africa, Europe. **Era:** early modern. **Reveal form:** Layered object investigation: three scripts, one decree. **Difficulty:** medium.

**Question.** In which year was the Rosetta Stone found?

**Answer: 1799.** French soldiers find the stone at Rashid (Rosetta) during the French invasion

- Definition: The year of discovery. The decree on the stone dates from 196 BC; the Greek text was first translated in 1803; Champollion announced decipherment in 1822. Sources disagree on the day in July.
- Precision: month (July); year used. Calendar: Gregorian.
- Discovery versus event: Discovery of the object. Not the date of the decree, not the decipherment.
- Corridor: 1790 to 1815.


**Free evidence** (what every player sees)

- *bound* By the end of that year, the French campaign in Egypt had already begun (28 June 1798).  
  Anchor: French invasion of Egypt begins, 28 June 1798. Sources: [French invasion of Egypt and Syria (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_campaign_in_Egypt_and_Syria). Level **V1**.
- *bound* By the end of that year, the French campaign in Egypt had not yet ended (2 September 1801).  
  Anchor: End of the French campaign in Egypt, 2 September 1801. Sources: [French invasion of Egypt and Syria (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_campaign_in_Egypt_and_Syria). Level **V1**.
- *relation* It was found one calendar year after the Battle of the Nile (1 to 3 August 1798).  
  Anchor: Battle of the Nile, 1-3 August 1798. Sources: [Battle of the Nile (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Nile). Level **V1**.

**Candidates after the two free bounds (C0):** 1798, 1799, 1800 (3 years).

**Uniqueness proof** (why only 1799 survives the relation):

- 1798 is +0 calendar years from Battle of the Nile (1798); the clue needs +1.
- 1800 is +2 calendar years from Battle of the Nile (1798); the clue needs +1.

**Paid clues**

- Nudge, 1 Insight, category *Politics*: By the end of that year, Napoleon had already left Egypt (23 August 1799).  
  Cuts 1798 from C0, leaves 2.  Sources: [French invasion of Egypt and Syria (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_campaign_in_Egypt_and_Syria). Level **V1**.
- Deep, 2 Insight, category *War*: By the end of that year, the Battle of Marengo had not yet been fought (14 June 1800).  
  Cuts 1800 from C0, leaves 2.  Sources: [Battle of Marengo (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Marengo). Level **V1**.

**Free context (cuts nothing):** The stone carries one decree in three scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic and Ancient Greek.


**Sample player explanation (free evidence only, zero Insight)**

1. The French invaded in 1798, so the stone was found in 1798 or later. They surrendered in 1801, so it was found by 1800. The candidates are 1798, 1799 and 1800.
2. The Battle of the Nile was in August 1798. One calendar year after is 1799.
3. Lock 1799.

**If the player misses.** 1798, 1799 and 1800 fit the bounds. Only 1799 is one calendar year after the Battle of the Nile (August 1798).

**Reveal.** Form: Layered object investigation: three scripts, one decree.

- *Found, made, read* (Layered object): Three dates, three different questions. The decree was made in 196 BC. The stone was found in July 1799. Its text was first read in translation in 1803, and the Egyptian scripts were transliterated in 1822. Sources: [Rosetta Stone (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_Stone).
- *Why the day is missing* (Note on dates): Accounts give 15 July, 19 July and, in one encyclopedia, August 1799. We only say 1799. Sources: [Rosetta Stone](https://www.britannica.com/print/article/509988) (not opened).

**Facts and verification**

- [V1] The stone was found in July 1799 by Pierre-François Bouchard during France's invasion of Egypt. (July 1799; month). Opened: [Rosetta Stone (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_Stone). Corroboration seen only in search summaries: [Rosetta Stone](https://www.britannica.com/print/article/509988) (not opened). Note: Search results give 15 July, 19 July and, in Britannica, August 1799. The year is stable; the day is not. Only the year is used.
- [V1] The decree on the stone was issued in 196 BC under Ptolemy V Epiphanes. (196 BC; year). Opened: [Rosetta Stone (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_Stone). Corroboration seen only in search summaries: none.
- [V1] The first complete translation of the Greek text was published in 1803. (1803; year). Opened: [Rosetta Stone (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_Stone). Corroboration seen only in search summaries: none.
